messages.subject: Finding SEs with createItem()
parts:
First off, let me just say you've done an amazing job with this R package, and a lot of us grad students (and professionals) are thrilled to be able to use it. 

Okay, my question: I'm not able to find standard errors with createItem(). It keeps kicking back the error below:

Error in Estep.mirt(pars = pars[[g]], tabdata = gtabdata, freq = 1L, CUSTOM.IND = CUSTOM.IND,  : 
  argument "full" is missing, with no default

Here is some code to reproduce the results - copied and pasted from the documentation with a small adjustment.

name <- 'old2PL'
par <- c(a = .5, b = -2)
est <- c(TRUE, TRUE)
P.old2PL <- function(par,Theta, ncat){
        a <- par[1]
        b <- par[2]
        P1 <- 1 / (1 + exp(-1*a*(Theta - b)))
        cbind(1-P1, P1)
}

x <- createItem(name, par=par, est=est, P=P.old2PL)
#So, let's estimate it!
dat <- expand.table(LSAT7)
sv <- mirt(dat, 1, c(rep('2PL',4), 'old2PL'), customItems=list(old2PL=x), pars = 'values')
tail(sv) #looks good
mod <- mirt(dat, 1, c(rep('2PL',4), 'old2PL'), SE.type='Fisher',SE=TRUE, customItems=list(old2PL=x))
coef(mod, printSE=TRUE)

Note that I added the SE.type='Fisher', SE=TRUE and the printSE=TRUE. The rest is straight from your documentation.

Can you explain a little about what the function is doing, and why it can't find standard errors? I'm looking forward to hearing from you. 
Thanks
Charlie

Hi Charlie,

Thanks for your kind words. You're right, this appears to be a bug in the code. However, if you really want to get at standard errors for now, the 'SEM' methods appears to work okay for custom item types. I'll try my hand at fixing these errors on the next major release (version 1.10 is scheduled to be released in a few weeks). Cheers.

Phil

Can you tell me a little more about what the function is doing? 
Does the IRF have to be from a particular family of models? How flexible is the function? 

The user defines how the likelihood is calculated, and then the function uses the same EM estimation engine (or MHRM) to find the parameters? I don't know how the function can set up the E-step without knowing the model. Don't you need to know the model to do the E-step?

Oh, and yes, the 'SEM' option appears to work, thank you again and I'll keep an eye out for the new release.

take care,
Charlie

messages.subject: Re: Finding SEs with createItem()
parts:
On Wed, Jun 10, 2015 at 10:53 PM, Charlie_Rutgers <charles.i...@gmail.com> wrote:
Can you tell me a little more about what the function is doing? 
Does the IRF have to be from a particular family of models? How flexible is the function?

You can fit any model you would like with createItem(), there really isn't a limit. And the next version will provide better support for things like itemfit(), M2(), information plots, etc, as well as a more modular way to add item types to the package directly (something other graduate students have been interested in doing as of late). The difficulty is not knowing the exact parametric form beforehand, which is why these models tend to be a lot slower.

The user defines how the likelihood is calculated, and then the function uses the same EM estimation engine (or MHRM) to find the parameters? I don't know how the function can set up the E-step without knowing the model. Don't you need to know the model to do the E-step?

Yes, and things like derivatives are taken care of for the most part (unless they are supplied manually, which would give much better performance). It's certain properties that are just too difficult to automate, like computing the cross-product/Louis information (which is best done with complied code; and even then they can be very time consuming).
Oh, and yes, the 'SEM' option appears to work, thank you again and I'll keep an eye out for the new release.

If you install the dev version from github, a number of others will work as well. Namely, the MHRM, SEM, BL, Complete, and Fisher. I won't be supporting the crossprod, sandwich and Louis for these models though....too complicated to say the least. Cheers.

Phil

take care,
Charlie
